r1-observability-1.summary: payments-api experienced a ~3.3x increase in p99 latency starting exactly at 2026-10-15T13:20:00+00:00, with no corresponding errors or traffic anomalies.

findings.statement: payments-api p99 latency rose from a baseline of ~370-395 ms to 1252.38 ms at 2026-10-15T13:20:00+00:00, peaking at 1485.07 ms.
payments-api request rate and error rate remained stable with no significant anomalies during the incident window.

open_questions: What downstream service or dependency is causing payments-api requests to slow down?

r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped dependency paths for payments-api and reviewed all changes across focus services over the last 7 days. Found a significant config change in ledger-service (query batch size increased from 100 to 1000) at 13:18 on 2026-10-15, which precedes the reported onset of latency issues (~13:20).

findings.statement: payments-api has synchronous dependencies on ledger-service, upi-gateway, fraud-service, and redis-cache, and an asynchronous dependency on event-bus.
upi-gateway depends on npci-switch and partner-bank-api.
ledger-service depends on ledger-db, and fraud-service depends on redis-cache.
A configuration change chg-8940 occurred on ledger-service at 2026-10-15T13:18:00+00:00 modifying the query batch size from 100 to 1000.
Minor feature flag and config changes occurred on payments-api and fraud-service days prior to the incident (chg-3458, chg-6174, chg-2932, chg-4033, chg-4326).
No changes were recorded for upi-gateway or partner-bank-api in the 7-day deployment window.

open_questions: Did the batch size change in ledger-service directly cause database or downstream latency affecting payments-api?
Were there any infrastructure or network events between coredns and ledger-db around 13:20?

r2-observability-1.summary: Following configuration change chg-8940 at 13:18, ledger-service and ledger-db both show a sharp increase in latency and CPU usage starting at 13:19, confirming performance degradation linked to the batch size increase.

findings.statement: ledger-service p99 latency increased starting at 2026-10-15T13:19:00+00:00, with baseline 121.05 ms and peak 975.46 ms.
ledger-service began logging slow ledger queries starting at 2026-10-15T13:19:22+00:00.
ledger-db p99 latency increased starting at 2026-10-15T13:19:00+00:00, moving from a baseline of 14.77 ms to a peak of 138.58 ms.
ledger-db CPU usage increased starting at 2026-10-15T13:19:00+00:00, peaking at 52.86%.
ledger-db logged slow SQL statements starting at 2026-10-15T13:19:06+00:00.
The performance degradation in ledger-service and ledger-db was triggered by the batch size increase configuration change chg-8940 at 13:18.

hypotheses.title: Ledger query batch size configuration change caused latency
hypotheses.mechanism: A configuration change chg-8940 increased the ledger query batch size from 100 to 1000 at 13:18 on 2026-10-15. This resulted in larger SQL operations against ledger-db starting at 13:19, causing p99 latency to rise in both ledger-db and ledger-service. Because payments-api makes synchronous calls to ledger-service, this downstream latency propagation directly drove up payments-api p99 latency starting at 13:20.

supporting.note: Configuration change modifying query batch size directly precedes the database and service latency increase.
ledger-service p99 latency increased immediately following the configuration change.
ledger-db p99 latency increased at the same time.
ledger-service logged slow ledger queries starting at 13:19.
ledger-db logged slow statements starting at 13:19.
payments-api latency spiked right after downstream ledger latency increased.
Synchronous dependency links payments-api performance directly to ledger-service.

contradicting.note: Error rate and request rate remained stable, indicating successful completion rather than failure or timeouts.

assumptions: Synchronous calls from payments-api wait for ledger-service transactions to complete, causing request duration to track the increased database and ledger-service latency.

hypotheses.title: Third-party UPI gateway or partner bank latency
hypotheses.mechanism: External partner banks or npci-switch experienced latency spikes, causing upi-gateway calls from payments-api to slow down and increasing overall p99 latency.

supporting.note: p99 latency increase matches external gateway slowness symptoms.

contradicting.note: An internal config change occurred precisely before onset, making internal config regression much more probable.
ledger-service also degraded at the exact same time, aligning with the internal config change.

assumptions: External vendors experienced latency simultaneously at 13:20, and the precise timing of ledger-service config change chg-8940 is a coincidence.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive telemetry and logs for ledger-service and ledger-db have been retrieved, confirming that ledger-service and ledger-db experienced immediate performance degradation starting at 13:19—precisely one minute after configuration change chg-8940 at 13:18. This directly propagates to payments-api at 13:20 via synchronous dependency dep:payments-api->ledger-service, cementing H1 as the root cause with high confidence.
